Jamal Musiala will be sidelined “until further notice” after suffering a muscle injury to his right hamstring, in another setback for the 23-year-old.

Musiala has struggled with repeated injury issues over the last two years as well as a neurological condition which has received enormous scrutiny in recent weeks.

He suffered a muscle tear in April 2025 and began suffering from absence seizures, which cause a brief and sudden lapse in awareness, the same month, two months after signing a contract extension with Bayern Munich.

Recent findings suggest that the condition was not made public knowledge until this summer, with Musiala experiencing two of these seizures during pre-season games. Absence seizures can be managed with daily medication, and other elite athletes, including England rugby player Tommy Freeman, have been able to continue professional sporting careers while experiencing the condition.

Over the same period Musiala has endured repeated injuries: he broke his fibula during the Club World Cup in 2025 and suffered a subsequent ankle injury, then had a metal plate removed from his foot after this summer’s World Cup.

He has only recently returned from an absence induced by a hamstring tear, coming off the bench against Koln in the Bundesliga after two months out. He made an appearance as a second-half substitute in Bayern’s surprise 2-1 defeat to Lille in the Champions League this week, but has now suffered another setback.

According to recent reports, bayern Munich announced on Friday: “FC Bayern’s medical department diagnosed Jamal Musiala with a muscle injury in his right thigh today. Musiala will be out until further notice. Get well soon, Jamal!”.

How Bayern have handled Musiala’s neurological condition has been heavily criticised after highly-publicised comments by several members of the club’s hierarchy.

Former board chairman Karl-Heinz Rummenigge cast doubt on the midfielder’s future, saying the “hefty sums of money” Musiala is paid are “not justifiable any longer”, and honorary president Uli Hoeness suggested his contract - which now runs until 2030 - should be reviewed if his illness and injury record prevents him returning to top form.

The comments sparked backlash, with players’ union Fifpro saying it was “deeply concerned” by the “pressure” placed on Musiala by such public remarks.

Stand-in captain Joshua Kimmich mentioned after the Lille defeat: “What I don’t understand is the way this is being communicated in public. It must never happen that the burden is placed on a player. The club is obviously the top priority and bigger than a player, but it’s not bigger than a person. That’s an absolute no-go and it is not Bayern-like.”.

Bayern have a raft of top players out with injuries including star striker Harry Kane, who tore ligaments in his ankle during the Koln game, as well as Michael Olise, Manuel Neuer, Luis Diaz and Serge Gnabry.

They sit second in the Bundesliga and 15th in the Champions League group phase table.

By the end of another utterly chaotic 90 minutes in the Manchester United soap opera, there was only one person who had endured a worse night than Senne Lammens.

Watching this game back will make for grim viewing for the United goalkeeper who, having been one of the club’s shining lights last season, is steadily becoming enveloped in a crisis of his own in this most torrid of campaigns.

Industry observers note that but Roberto Rosetti, Uefa’s chief refereeing officer, might also want to sit Szymon Marciniak down after this and pick over the Polish official’s own nightmare performance. Marciniak denied United two goals, both of which should have stood, and in doing so ended up shining an even more brutal lens on Lammens’s calamitous display.

Sources indicate that united’s Belgian goalkeeper was responsible for both of Sporting’s goals. He needlessly conceded a penalty in the first half, after a rush of blood to the head, that was converted by Luis Suárez, just 75 seconds after he had saved a spot-kick from the Sporting striker.

United had recovered from those bewildering few minutes to lead early in the second half, courtesy of two goals from captain Bruno Fernandes against his old club.

Recent findings suggest that but, 10 minutes from time, Lammens committed the kind of howler that becomes worse and worse with every viewing. In doing so, he handed Sporting an equaliser and ensured United remain without an away win this season.

Lammens could have come to meet Iván Fresneda’s cross 100 times and probably dropped the ball only once. It was his and United’s misfortune that it should happen here. Suárez could barely believe his luck, although his finish was still accomplished, an acrobatic overhead kick from close range.

Recent findings suggest that one of the stars of last season for United, Lammens is being dragged down with the rest of them this time around. He had looked hesitant from the moment he was almost caught dealing with a back-pass by Suárez in the opening minutes. It set the tone for what was to come.

As if Mauricio Pochettino did not already have enough on his plate, United’s new head coach now has a goalkeeper problem.

Recent findings suggest that of course, this would not have been as costly a night for Lammens had Marciniak not made such a mess of things himself. United may have been their own worst enemies again, but there was little doubting Sporting were given a helping hand here by some truly wretched refereeing.

The worst of it was the denial of a perfectly legitimate equaliser late in the first half after Youri Tielemans was penalised for a perceived foul – it was nothing of the sort – that the referee had initially not blown for.

And then moments after Suarez made it 2-2, the Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira flapped at Fernandes’s corner and punched the ball into his own net. Kaique’s blunder was already in motion by the time Patrick Dorgu barged into Kaique. But Marciniak was ordered to the pitch-side monitor by Piotr Lasyk, the VAR, and from there, he weakly decided Kaique had been infringed upon by Dorgu. It was a significant let-off for the goalkeeper and the hosts.

To compounded United’s frustrations, they were then reduced to 10 men late on when Tielemans, who had been booked for protesting over the first disallowed goal, received a second yellow card. It means United have now had four red cards and conceded five penalties in their last five games and, four weeks shy of Christmas, are still searching for a win on the road.

The irony was that, amidst the chaos, there was a lot Pochettino will have liked about the performance. It was far from perfect but United at least had a structure, coherence and confidence about them for long periods. But for Lammens’s shocker and some dubious refereeing, United would surely have claimed just a fourth win this season.

The problem with this United side is they never seem too far away from an act of self-sabotage. Pochettino insisted on the eve of this game that his team were not fragile, but that assessment was challenged in the crazy 160 seconds when United conceded not one but two penalties.

In truth, they could feel hard done to by the award of the first in the 29th minute. Geny Catamo went down far too easily – and very late – after Lisandro Martínez swung out a leg. There was contact but it was of the very minimal variety. Martínez rushed off to Marciniak to remonstrate but his pleas fell on deaf ears. There was a sense of justice, then, when Lammens saved Suárez’s feeble penalty.

You would have thought that would be a confidence booster for Lammens, but in no time he had gone from hero to zero, with worse to follow.

Industry observers note that A ball was swept in behind Noussair Mazraoui and Maximiliano Araújo gave chase. There was no need for Lammens to come careering out of goal but that is what he did. When he clumsily blocked off Araújo in the process, Marciniak wasted little time brandishing a yellow card and pointing to the spot. This time Suárez made no mistake from 12 yards.

What will please Pochettino is United did not crumble again from there. In fact, they rallied and would soon be nursing a sense of injustice for the second time in four days.

Already outraged by the circumstances around Leny Yoro’s rescinded red card against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, Pochettino now had to contend with some perverse refereeing from Marciniak.

“He wasn’t making his bed a year ago, now he has to cook his own dinner and get himself to training.”.

He’s thrown him under the bus, there.

Wandering around the Jose Alvalade Stadium before kick-off and Cristiano Ronaldo’s face and old No 7 is pasted on the outside of the building.

How Pochettino would love a prime Ronaldo in his team but we’re in as very different era now to the one when United went into this competition with a firm expectation of winning it. It’s two wins and two defeats so far in the Champions League for United this season although you suspect they’d be happy to come away from here with a point.

It has been revealed that they have yet to win away from home this season and Sporting, who have won three of their four European games, are third in the Portuguese league. Watch out for Colombia striker Luis Suarez and Italy midfielder Issa Doumbia, who have six goals between them in the Champions League this term.

Sporting XI: Kaique, Fresneda, Quaresma, Inacio, Araujo, Andersen, Altimira, Doumbia, Catamo, Suarez, Luis Guilherme.

Subs: Rui Silva, Callai, Ioannidis, Simoes, Vagiannidis, Zalazar, Irankunda, Lima, Derry, Ba, Felicissimo, Goncalves.

Mauricio Pochettino has made four changes to the side that were beaten 4-0 at Anfield by Liverpool. One of those is enforced, with the suspended Matheus Cunha making way for Joshua Zirkzee, who gets his first start of the season. Harry Maguire comes in for Matthijs de Ligt, who was abysmal against Liverpool, and Noussair Mazraoui replaces Diogo Dalot. Amad Diallo is in over Patrick Dorgu. Mainoo and Tielemans have struggled as a partnership all season but Pochettino again persists with that midfield pairing with Bruno Fernandes ahead of them.

Manchester United XI: Lammens; Yoro, Maguire, Martinez, Mazraoui; Tilemans, Mainoo; Amad, Fernandez, Mbeumo; Zirkzee.

Subs: Darlow, Heaton, Amass, Dalot, De Ligt, Heaven, Shaw, Santos, Mount, Lacey.

They need to finish 24th or higher to avoid elimination. They only have two fewer points (after four games) in the Champions League than they do in the Premier League (after 11).

Few Manchester United fans expected a positive result from Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge at Anfield, but the bar will not be set so low for Sporting in the Champions League this evening.

It has been revealed that the manner of the 4-0 defeat against Liverpool, even accounting for Leny Yoro’s early red card, was dispiriting but not unexpected. The next few weeks will reveal how Pochettino intends to get a grip on the job.

When it comes to United’s Champions League prospects, the comeback win over Roma at the tail-end of Michael Carrick’s tenure made their position less perilous, but avoiding outright elimination is the first target.

United are 19th in the table, with the top 24 teams going through. Those between ninth and 24th go into a play-off round before the last 16. After Sporting away, United host RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich before a trip to Villarreal so there are stiff tests to come.

Sporting are well-placed after three wins from four, but their Champions League schedule is rather one-sided: in their final three matches they travel to Roma, before playing Barcelona and Manchester City. They reached the quarter-finals of the competition last season, losing narrowly to Arsenal over two legs.

They are third in their league, having been weakened by the summer sales of Geovany Quenda (to Chelsea), Morten Hjulmand (to Atletico Madrid) and Ousmane Diomande (to Nottingham Forest). The vast majority of goals are scored by Colombian striker Luis Suárez.

According to recent reports, bruno Fernandes, United’s captain, returns to his former club tonight and there is hope Luke Shaw could be back at left-back. Pochettino must decide whether or not to stick with Matthijs de Ligt, who was extremely rusty at Anfield but may need the minutes.

Yoro’s one-game suspension was overturned by the FA, and he would have been available for this one in any case.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • US tech firm Nvidia said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO "effective immediately.".
  • This follows just a matter of days after his resignation after admitting to extramarital affairs, reportedly including a dalliance with a woman who was a Chinese intelligence asset.
  • The board unanimously decided that his return was in the "best interests of the company," Nvidia stated, adding that it was satisfied that Huang had demonstrated his "candor and ability to lead.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

US tech firm Nvidia said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO "effective immediately.".

This follows just a matter of days after his resignation after admitting to extramarital affairs, reportedly including a dalliance with a woman who was a Chinese intelligence asset.

The board unanimously decided that his return was in the "best interests of the company," Nvidia stated, adding that it was satisfied that Huang had demonstrated his "candor and ability to lead.".

Meanwhile, the 63-year-old said in a statement that he was "honored" to return to the company and that he would take on the renewed responsibility "with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.".

He thanked interim CEO Colette Kress, who is set to return to her role as chief financial officer.

Recent findings suggest that "I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support," Huang noted. "Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work.".

US President Donald Trump rapidly commented on the development online, saying it was the "correct and proper decision" and referring to Huang by his first name as a "Great Patriot and National Treasure.".

"The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security," Trump wrote, also saying that the US had no evidence of him engaging in unlawful conduct.

Huang liked to flaunt his personal relationship with Trump. He was reportedly influential in convincing the US president to allow the export of higher-quality Nvidia chips to China that are useful in AI development than other US officials and entrepreneurs endorsed.

The decision was confirmed as trading started for the upcoming week in New York.

The stock price of what investors deem the world's most valuable manufacturer has nosedived amid the scandal, with Nvidia's stock price falling from almost $220 (roughly €200) per share in late October to around $125 per share at the end of last week.

The announcement prompted a rapid early-morning rally on Wall Street, including Nvidia stocks rising back into a region between $160 and $170.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Huang quit earlier this month after admitting to extramarital affairs in a note to employees.

This concession came amid widespread reporting in the US linking him romantically to one woman in particular, who was running a major Nvidia client called Megaspeed based in Singapore and who was said to be an asset of Chinese intelligence services.

Her company is also suspected of diverting chips not approved for export to China to the Chinese market, circumventing US sanctions.

It has been revealed that while these allegations have not been proven, they appeared to be based on the assessments of US and other western intelligency agencies, and to be information that was known for around a year. One possible indication of this was Singapore refusing the Chinese national entry into the country earlier in 2026.

In a recent development, well that was a busy year! What started with non-league Macclesfield knocking FA Cup holders Crystal Palace out in the third round of the competition, ended with Harry Kane lifting the Ballon d’Or in London.

Roberto De Zerbi has hailed Luca Williams-Barnett’s latest contract as a clear sign of Tottenham’s ambition.

Williams-Barnett marked his full debut for Spurs with a goal and assist in Saturday’s 2-0 win over Ipswich to justify the growing hype around the highly-rated 18-year-old.

It was followed by a newly introduced long-term contract for the teenager on Tuesday, which is understood to run until 2031, and ahead of Sunday’s trip to Sunderland De Zerbi stressed the importance of keeping hold of him.

“It’s great news for us, the extension of his contract, because if you see other massive teams, big clubs, they are losing young talent in the same situations,” De Zerbi stated.

“We have to say thanks to the club, because I think it was an notable step for us, for the pitch, for the football, but also for the fans, because I think we gave a great signal with this extension of the contract.

It has been revealed that “And if the agent of Luca, if the family of Luca, accept to stay and to extend the contract, it’s because they believe in the Tottenham project. So I think the credit is for the club.”.

Williams-Barnett looks to be in line for another start at Sunderland due to the absence of several attacking players.

De Zerbi added: “You have to analyse many things.

“I think he is ready to play because he is a mature guy, he has the personality to play in every stadium, every game, but we have to analyse everything he has done this week.

“The debut in the first XI, the goal, the assist, the extension of his contract. Everything is for the best. For us, for him, for the club.”.

De Zerbi used Dejan Kulusevski as an example for Williams-Barnett to follow and the Sweden playmaker could start one of Tottenham’s three matches over the next week after a 17-month absence with a serious knee injury.

“I am thinking to start maybe not now, but I think we are very close to start a game,” De Zerbi added.

Sources indicate that “Deki is working well. I watched his games in the national team just to understand the physical condition.

“He played the first game as a winger and the second game as a number 10 and especially in the second game he played very well, but we have to be good to understand the right moment to put him on the pitch.

“I think medical staff, physical staff, they are working very well with him and we can’t lose any time, but we can’t take any risk because he is a special player.”.

While Kulusevski is close to a start, Tottenham are set to be without Savio for the rest of 2026 and beyond due to a hamstring glitch sustained late on against Ipswich.

In a recent development, de Zerbi remarked: “I don’t know, 50 days, 60 days, 80 days, I don’t know. When he comes back I think he will be crucial for us for the last step of the season.”.

Bournemouth's nine-game winning streak faced one of its sternest tests in Spain on Thursday night.

Marco Rose's men found themselves trailing to an Iago Aspas opener at Balaidos and reduced to 10 men following Bafode Diakite’s first-half dismissal, but refused to buckle.

Second-half strikes from Alvaro Rodríguez and Rayan sealed a remarkable Europa League comeback, extending a run of form that has seen the Cherries sweep aside AC Milan, Manchester United, Aston Villa and the like.

Away from the Vitality Stadium, Bournemouth’s form hasn't received the wider acclaim it warrants - perhaps because they aren't a 'big six' club.

Recent findings suggest that context makes this run all the more extraordinary because only 18 years ago, in the summer of 2008, Bournemouth were staring into the abyss at the bottom of League Two, slapped with a 17-point deduction after failing to exit administration. The club was fighting to remain in the Football League.

The Cherries of present day are a winning machine, domestically and on the continent, even after losing influential manager Andoni Iraola to Liverpool in the summer.

Industry observers note that the success of their dugout transition comes down to decisive governance. When it became apparent that Iraola had outgrown the club, owner and chairman Bill Foley - the American businessman who bought 100 per cent of the club from Maxim Demin via Black Knight Football Club in December 2022 - and president of football operations Tiago Pinto moved early.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Rose’s appointment was rubber-stamped well before pre-season began, giving the former RB Leipzig and Borussia Dortmund boss a full summer to embed.

Under Foley and Pinto, Bournemouth’s recruitment machine has become the envy of most Premier League peers. In recent windows, their scouting network has consistently uncovered high-upside talent capable of generating massive resale value, from Illia Zabarnyi and Dean Huijsen to Milos Kerkez, before reinvesting shrewdly to build a squad that is now brimming with depth.

Rose now presides over a balanced group with what feels like at least two Premier League-level options in every position. It blends seasoned Premier League campaigners like Lewis Cook, Ryan Christie and Tyler Adams with European pedigree in new centre-back Antonio Silva, plus young flair in Amine Adli and Rayan.

Perhaps most surprising of all, this record-breaking 10-game winning run has been achieved without talismanic forward Eli Junior Kroupi, which is a testament to the collective strength the club has forged.

According to recent reports, unlike Brighton’s Tony Bloom or Brentford’s Matthew Benham, Bournemouth have not relied on an owner with a background in professional gambling, analytics and mathematical models. Foley’s multi-club network and Pinto’s acumen as a top football executive has combined traditional scouting, a bit of data analytics, but most importantly decisive succession planning and smart squad-building.

Recent findings suggest that for clubs up and down the English league pyramid, Bournemouth are proof that you don't need state-backed billions or algorithms to punch above your weight. With coherent leadership, aligned recruitment and an acknowledgement of the need to plan two steps ahead, even a club once deducted 17 points in the fourth tier looks on course to maybe even conquer Europe.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that to that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon.

Recent findings suggest that to that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal.

"We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter," Aymeric Goyer, associate professor at OSU's Department of Botany and Plant Pathology, said in a statement. "That's an important step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the moon.".

Recent findings suggest that to grow the spuds, the scientists used five different materials that are similar to regolith, the dust and rocks that cover the moon's surface. The moon contains various regions with unique surface makeups, so the materials they used simulated regolith from both lunar mare and lunar highland regions.

The secret ingredient was vermicompost, a soil that's rich in nutrients. The team added different levels of vermicompost to the simulated regolith to grow the potatoes. They figured out that fake regolith mixed with 30 percent vermicompost worked about as well as growing potatoes with regular soil.

"We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith by reducing plant exposure to harmful compounds," David Handy, a postdoctoral researcher in Goyer's lab, said in the same statement.

In a recent development, the idea is that astronauts in the future could bring a little nutrient-rich soil with them and mix it with regolith to grow potatoes. After all, it'd cost a ton to ship all that food from Earth.

NASA funding supported this research.

Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

Manchester United's problems will not be solved until the Glazers leave the club, according to former England international Lianne Sanderson.

Despite feeling optimistic about Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment, Sanderson believes the ownership situation leaves a significant obstacle for managers to have success at Old Trafford.

Manchester United currently sit 19th in the Premier League table with just eight points from 11 games, and the club's struggles have left lifelong supporter Sanderson feeling increasingly disconnected from a team she has followed since childhood.

With Manchester United languishing in the relegation zone, Sanderson believes the problems run much deeper than the performances on the pitch.

Since Sir Alex Ferguson left in 2013, Manchester United have had 12 different managers. Michael Carrick’s departure earlier this month was followed by the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino, someone who is a friend of Sanderson.

Industry observers note that “Nothing is going to change until the ownership leave and that's the reality of the situation,” Sanderson said. “You can't blame the coach.

"It wasn't Michael Carrick's fault. I love Poch, he's a good friend of mine and I want him to succeed.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Industry observers note that "But I don't think they fully realise how big of a job this is going to be. I think every newly introduced manager thinks they can come into Man United and be that saviour.

"But the ownership are the biggest problem. Since INEOS came in, there's not been progress. I felt excited when Sir Jim Ratcliffe came in as a minority owner, but the Glazers are the biggest problem.

"Until they go, Manchester United are going to be in this situation.".

Sanderson's frustration is particularly personal given her lifelong connection to the club.

Despite being part of Arsenal’s Champions League winning team in 2007, the former striker has been a United fan since childhood and said she would have loved to finish her playing career at United, had the club established a women's team earlier.

“I feel really disassociated with Man United right now, I just feel so gutted with where our club is at,” Sanderson added.

In a recent development, “Manchester United is like my religion. I often go in the away end because I love the club and I love being with the fans, it’s more meaningful.

According to recent reports, “When I was five and I saw Eric Cantona play, I fell in love with Man United. That's why I love the club.

"It would have been easier for me to support Arsenal, obviously. It's a bit awkward when I go in the away end at the Emirates and some of the stewards recognise me.

"It's funny that they've got my picture outside the Emirates and I'm walking into the away end!".

Despite her concerns, Sanderson remains hopeful that Pochettino can turn things around, although she believes significant recruitment will be required.

The former England international suggested there are only around four players in the current squad worthy of keeping.

"I hope Pochettino can be the one to change things, I'm optimistic,” she added. “It can't get any worse, but the team are fighting relegation and that's the reality.

"I saw someone the other day say: ‘Would you take relegation in order to get the ownership out?’ That’s how strongly the fanbase feel about this and I never thought I'd ever feel that way.

According to recent reports, "But I hope Poch can turn it around. They need a big transfer window to do that.".

Renee Slegers has left her role as head coach of Arsenal following a difficult start to the Women’s Super League season for the north London club.

The Gunners occupy sixth place in the WSL standings, sitting 12 points behind leaders Chelsea after 11 matches, and remain winless at home in the league this term.

The Dutch manager assumed the role from Jonas Eidevall, initially on an interim basis, two years ago before guiding Arsenal to Champions League glory in May 2025.

A statement on arsenal.com read: "We can confirm Renee Slegers has left her position as head coach of our women’s first team by mutual consent.

"Renee departs following a disappointing start to the 2026-27 season, with assistant coach Aaron D’Antino also leaving the club.

In a recent development, "The process of appointing a successor is under way and we will revision in due course. Assistant coach Melissa Clarke-Reed will take charge of the team in the interim period.

"Everyone at Arsenal would like to thank Renee and Aaron for their contributions to the club and wish them every success in their future careers.".

Pressure had been mounting on Slegers, particularly with Arsenal struggling to convert in front of goal, and her final match ended in a goalless draw against West Ham last Sunday.

Gunners director of women’s football Clare Wheatley mentioned: "It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renee, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here.

"In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural Fifa Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal, with close support from Aaron.

"After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level and change is necessary.".

Arsenal have two weeks until their next fixture due to the international break, with England set to face Ukraine in a two-legged playoff as Sarina Wiegman’s side aim to secure their place at next year’s World Cup.

Once the international break finishes, Arsenal will return to action without Slegers when they travel to Everton on 11 December.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When India's world chess champion, Dommaraju Gukesh, faced reporters at the pre-tournament press conference in Geneva on Sunday, there was no sign of the youthful, carefree energy one might expect from a 20-year-old.

"I don't think I'm here to defend anything—I'm here to win it all over again," he said.

Starting November 24, Gukesh will be facing challenger Jakhovir Sindarov of Uzbekistan for a purse of $2.5 million (€2.3m) in the World Chess Championship.

According to recent reports, gukesh captured the title in 2024, making him the youngest-ever world champion at just 18. Since then, however, things have not as gone well for the player known for his exceptional calculation skills and a penchant for risky moves. He currently languishes in 26th place in the FIDE world rankings.

Sindarov, who has climbed to number four in the world, told reporters that he only began training "seriously" last year and has learned a lot from observing the reigning world champion.

"He has a very good strength in typical positions, his calculation is very good, and Gukesh can fight until the end," Sindarov noted.

Former world champion Viswanathan Anand, who was also one of the world's best players as a teenager, is not completely surprised by Gukesh's lack of form over the past two years.

In a recent development, "He became the world champion (very young). So suddenly the responsibility is shifted onto you and even expectations," Anand told DW.

"Clearly he has deficiencies in his chess as is normal for someone who's 20, he's not had time to experience a lot.".

By the time he became India's first world champion, Anand was 37 – ancient by the age-standards of today's top players.

"With powerful chess software and global connectivity, it is easier for young players today to reach the top level," Jan Gustafsson, coach of Germany's national chess team, told DW.

"Online chess provides many more learning opportunities for talented players," added Gustafsson, who sees the recent movement at the top of the rankings as a "generational shift.".

While Norway's Magnus Carlsen, long considered the greatest player of all time, remains number one in the world rankings, he rarely plays classical chess anymore and gave up his world championship title after declining to defend it in 2023.

Now, young players—particularly from Asia—are pushing to the forefront. Alongside Gukesh and Sindarov, players such as Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa from India and Nodirbek Abdusattorov of Uzbekistan—an emerging chess powerhouse—are considered contenders to win a world championship in the not-too-distant future.

"Broad social acceptance and state support ensure that children can focus on chess at a very early stage," Gustafsson noted.

According to recent reports, another contender is Germany's Vincent Keymer, who at 22 is number nine in the world and well established among the world's elite. Most recently, Keymer and his teammates won a bronze medal at the World Team Championship, often referred to as the "Chess Olympiad.".

Why Cambridgeshire derby could be season-defining

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Robbie Savage's Peterborough United will seek to defend a long unbeaten home record in the Cambridgeshire derby when Neil Harris's U's visit London Road.
  • Local derbies are always special, but none more so than when they have the ability to shape the narrative of a season.
  • Robbie Savage's Peterborough United welcome Neil Harris' Cambridge United to London Road with both at something of a crossroads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robbie Savage's Peterborough United will seek to defend a long unbeaten home record in the Cambridgeshire derby when Neil Harris's U's visit London Road.

History, tradition, bragging rights.

Local derbies are always special, but none more so than when they have the ability to shape the narrative of a season. This much is true of Saturday's Cambridgeshire derby (12:30 GMT).

Robbie Savage's Peterborough United welcome Neil Harris' Cambridge United to London Road with both at something of a crossroads.

Sources indicate that at stake for Posh? Their League One status. Despite an impressive win at Plymouth Argyle last time out, they remain 22nd in the table and need results to avoid a battle against the drop being the defining theme of their season.

As for the U's, the derby presents an opportunity to regain momentum. After October's 2-1 win at Barnsley they were one point off top spot, but failure to pick up three points in any of their five league games since leaves them caught between play-off contention and mid-table drift.

The derby also carries the weight of recent history, with the emotional baggage greater for the U's.

They have lost each of their past seven away league games against Peterborough, losing those matches by a combined 20-3 scoreline.

Indeed, they have not won at London Road since an FA Cup tie in 1994-95, while their wait for a league win at their rivals' home extends to 1990.

Savage, appointed last month, said his side were well aware of their responsibility for continuing that record.

"We don't want to be the group that loses to Cambridge at home, first time in 30 years I think it would be," he stated.

Industry observers note that "We don't want to be that group. We want to put three, four, five past them and win the game. Even if it's 1-0, it doesn't matter.

"It's all about winning, don't care we win, just win the game.".

Robbie Savage: 'We want to turn the county blue'.

It has been revealed that the victory at Plymouth ended a four-game wait for a win, and Savage said the onus was on his side to back it up on derby day. If they do, they know they will have secured successive league victories for the first time since February.

"This game is at the top of the mountain," he stated.

It has been revealed that "No doubt about it. The players will be up for it, we've shown them videos of the previous games, we've got fans sending messages.

"We're doing everything we can to make them realise how massive this game is. It's not another game, it's the derby. A great game.

"Neil knows what it means. We're two passionate managers. He's done far better than me as a manager so far, so hats off to him. But we both want to win.

"They will bring 1,600 fans and we need to show Cambridge that we want to county to be blue.".

Neil Harris: 'We'll attack the game like no other'.

While this derby is latest territory for Savage, Harris comes armed with the memory of defeat in his only previous taste of the tie in a season than ultimately ended with relegation for the U's.

After securing a return to the third-tier in 2025-26 - and having made a competitive start to this campaign - there is no shortage of motivation to deliver a long-awaited win for his side.

"It is a one-off fixture," he told BBC Look East.

"There is a slightly different feel and mentality to it, but it means a hell of a lot to a hell of a lot of people.

It has been revealed that "It means a lot to get bragging rights over a direct opponent. It's key to get back to our highest standards.".

Posh have lost just one of their past 12 league games against Cambridge United, winning their past four in succession.

But with Savage's side in a precarious league position, there is optimism among fans that their 36-year long wait to celebrate a league win at London Road could finally arrive.

"It's about playing with heart and emotion, but brains as well," added Harris.

"We understand the importance of the fixture, I understand it as a driven manager. It's about trying to make sure we make our fans proud.".

Arsenal legend Thierry Henry claims his former club are the only side right now showing control in the Premier League title race, dismissing the hype around Liverpool while pointing to high-flying Brighton as an overlooked threat.

Mikel Arteta’s side sit clear at the summit heading into Sunday’s showdown against Manchester City at the Emirates Stadium, where a victory would hand the Gunners a sizeable cushion over one of their fiercest rivals.

While Liverpool’s 4-0 demolition of Manchester United last weekend, and Man City's faltering form, led some pundits to anoint Andoni Iraola’s Reds as Arsenal’s closest challengers, Henry believes the weekly narrative around title contenders has been too reactive.

Speaking this week, via Betway, the Frenchman argued that Arsenal’s consistency sets them apart from the chasing pack, even if he expects the picture to shift again before the end of the campaign.

"No disrespect to anybody, but the only team that looks somewhat in control of games is Arsenal," Henry stated.

"Every month we talk about a new challenger. At the beginning of the season, everyone thought Arsenal had no challengers.

Industry observers note that "Then Man City went on a run of winning seven in a row, and they were seen as the challengers. Now City don’t win in four, and Liverpool look like the challenger. Nobody seems to talk about Brighton, but they are there as well. We will see.

"We can mention the game against Brighton or 25 minutes in the second half against Newcastle, but Arsenal do look like the most consistent team. Challengers come and go, and who knows who will win the league at the end of the day? But Arsenal look solid at the moment.".

Henry’s mention of Brighton highlights just how impressive the Seagulls have been so far, with Maxim De Cuyper and Pascal Gross inspiring a side boasting the league's best defensive record.

Arsenal's immediate focus is getting back to winning ways on Sunday afternoon after being held to a 2-2 draw by Newcastle last weekend. Having almost surrendered their advantage to City during last season’s run-in, Arteta’s men know better than anyone that early control counts for little unless they deliver when the biggest rivals come to town.

After an ill-advised interview earlier this week, Fofana followed that up with a string of mistakes which led to Nottingham Forest’s second goal.

Forest have secured 11 of their 12 points against clubs in the perceived “Big Six” and Aston Villa, who are competing in the Champions League, and did not deserve the scoreline to be as close.

Alonso is the latest Chelsea manager to become embroiled in chaos before Christmas and four defeats from five league matches will not make happy reading for the hierarchy.

His defence appear to be nervous wrecks and in his desperation to toughen them up he opted to play Moisés Caicedo in what was a peculiar line-up.

Chelsea have conceded 23 goals in the league and until they improve that record, Alonso will find it impossible to retain the club’s backing.

Recent findings suggest that “Everyone in the club needs to stick together and we have to deal with it,” he said. “We are going through a difficult moment with solidity and confidence, we need to find solutions.

“Everyone in the team is needed and I am thinking about the next games and we will see [if Fofana is picked for the next game]. We need to support everyone and if we don’t, things will get more complicated.”.

Forest responded after their insipid performance at Bournemouth last weekend to secure another notable home result for Oliver Glasner.

He must be hoping that Forest’s owner, Evangelos Marinakis, turns up for every game.

Marinakis was in attendance for only the second time this season and, on his last visit, witnessed a stirring victory over Manchester City.

Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice to win the private battle of the England No 10s, with Chelsea’s Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers both ineffective.

Chelsea are never far away from a crisis and this feels like a major night for Xabi Alonso.

Three defeats in the last four Premier League games, including a thrashing by Leeds in their last match, has cranked up the pressure.

This was always likely to be a long-term project, however, and Chelsea remain convinced Alonso will lead them into a bright new era.

It has been revealed that until then, there are going to be some tricky times ahead. Chelsea are as wildly unpredictable as the team they face this evening at the City Ground.

They would leapfrog Coventry regardless of the margin of victory, as they already have a better goal difference.

A draw would see them remain 17th, while a really heavy defeat might see them fall to 18th.

Glasner conceded, in his own press conference, that he had hoped for better results so far this season.

He stated: “We wanted and expected more to be honest, but it is still early. We look at what we need to improve and work on it. I’m no magician, I have no dust I can spread at the training ground.

Industry observers note that “From my experience, everything is hard work and we need to improve our individual mistakes and defence. We need to improve our efficiency in attack and set pieces. We still haven’t scored from a set piece.”.

He added that the club wanted a good atmosphere for the evening kick-off, saying that, “is what we want and need. Friday night under the flood lights - it’s crucial. Our fans want a great weekend.”.

Earlier in the week, Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana said he could now “laugh” about a recent penalty miss against Liverpool in the Carabao Cup.

While the statement went down badly amongst some supporters, Fofana has apologised, and Alonso told a pre-match press conference he was ready to move on.

He told journalists: “Absolutely, we have addressed that with him and for sure it was unfortunate.

“He apologised, he knows it was not right the moment, it was not right the content, we are here to take things seriously and he remarked that it’s not going to be repeated and we know that it’s something that we don’t want, these kind of things, and they are not going to be repeated for sure.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea.

The City Ground hosts the Premier League clash tonight, with two sides who are both falling short of expectations.

Forest head coach Oliver Glasner brought with him a sense of optimism after he left Crystal Palace, but the club are just outside the bottom three, sitting in 17th position with only nine points. As things stand, they are only clear of 18th-placed Sunderland because of superior goal difference.

In a recent development, beneath them, Glasner’s former club Palace are bottom, two points away from them, and then Manchester United come in 19th, a single point behind. With Thomas Frank and Mauricio Pochettino now installed at Selhurst Park and Old Trafford, respectively, the pressure could soon be felt yet more keenly.

There have been flashes of encouragement, with a 3-1 win over Manchester City in early November, spearheaded by a brace from Liam Delap, who left Chelsea in the summer. However, last Saturday they lost 2-0 at Bournemouth to dent any nascent momentum, and the match was the sixth in 11 league games where the club have failed to score. Forest have scored nine times this season, with only Sunderland having a worse record in attack.

Chelsea’s Xabi Alonso has also endured a tough time of late. They were trounced 4-1 against Leeds United at home on Saturday, despite taking the lead in the first half.

That worrying collapse was the fourth loss in five league matches, and it followed a 1-0 defeat against Sunderland at the Stadium of Light before the recent international break.

There is speculation that Chelsea will move for a central defender in January, with 20 goals conceded in the Premier League so far.

According to recent reports, chelsea are right now in eighth place in the league with 16 points, five points behind Liverpool in fourth. Tonight, they could leapfrog Bournemouth, who are in fifth, two points ahead of them. Another loss, though, could see them in the bottom half once the weekend’s fixtures are completed.

Wesley Fofana had a night to forget for Chelsea at Nottingham Forest as he gave away a penalty and was booed by his own fans at the end of a week where he courted controversy.

The Blues defender, who has been singled out for poor performances during the team’s bad run, needed a strong showing, having spoken for almost two hours with French YouTuber Zack Nani on a range of topics in a controversial, unauthorised interview.

Fofana admitted that he came close to quitting football whilst he was sidelined with an anterior cruciate injury, while also appearing to joke about missing his penalty during last month’s Carabao Cup shootout defeat to Liverpool.

He apologised for the interview and boss Xabi Alonso mentioned the matter was closed, but Friday’s Premier League game was a bad one for him.

The visiting supporters consistently jeered the centre-back when he was in possession in the first half. Fofana and his teammates endured a tough start at the City Ground as they fell behind to Igor Jesus’ brilliant fifth-minute strike.

A bad night got worse in the early stages of the second half when Fofana brought down Liam Delap for a penalty that Morgan Gibbs-White converted to double Forest’s lead.

He was substituted soon after, following chants from travelling Blues fans of “f*** off Fofana, you’re not wanted here.”.

Emmanuel Emegha did score to halve the deficit but Gibbs-White’s second goal restored Forest’s healthy advantage and although another late Emegha strike saw the Blues pile on the pressure to try and snatch an injury-time equaliser, they ultimately suffered a 3-2 loss that their poor performance deserved.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor's Note: The November full supermoon dazzled stargazers with a spectacular show overnight on Nov. 24. Check out our photo wrap article to see spectacular images of the "Beaver Moon" captured from around the world.

Recent findings suggest that get ready stargazers! The full "Beaver supermoon" rises in the eastern sky, offering up a spectacular display shortly after sunset tonight (Nov. 24). Here's what you need to know.

It has been revealed that november's full moon occurs at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk passes opposite the sun in our sky, making it appear fully lit from our perspective. The November full moon is often referred to as the Beaver Moon because it rises around the time the small mammals are hard at work building their lodges in preparation for the winter.

In a recent development, viewers in the U.S. can even get a detailed look at the full moon ahead of local moonrise thanks to a free supermoon livestream from the Virtual Telescope Project (VTP), starting at 10:30 a.m. EST (1530 GMT) today. The stream will feature live views of the lunar disk captured from the VTP's robotic telescopes in Manciano, Italy, weather permitting.

According to recent reports, the Beaver Moon is also set to be a dazzling supermoon, because it turns full as the natural satellite passes within 90% of perigee, when it is at its closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit. A supermoon's proximity can make it appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than the most distant full moon of the year, which is colloquially known as a "micro-moon".

Sources indicate that november's full moon will be below the horizon for stargazers in the U.S. at the moment it turns full. Instead, viewers in America should look out for the moon shortly after sunset on Nov. 24, as it looms low over the eastern horizon.

Try covering the lunar disk with your thumb to block out the worst of its glare, and you may just be able to spot to blue-white lights of the Pleiades open star cluster glimmering less than 10 degrees away — roughly the width of your clenched fist held at arm's length.

If you miss the full moon on Nov. 24, don't worry as the moon will appear full to the casual observer for a couple more nights, so there's no excuse to miss it! Remember to check out Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location.

You may see the moon turn a striking orange-yellow hue as it rises because sunlight reflected from its disk passes through more of Earth's atmosphere, which scatters shorter bluer wavelengths of light and allows more red and orange light to reach our eyes in a process called Rayleigh scattering.

This is a fantastic go-to telescope with a 4-inch aperture and can help you rapidly find a steady view of the moon. Check out our full Celestron Nexstar 4SE review for more.

The supermoon will also appear particularly large while close to the horizon, as a phenomenon called the "moon illusion" tricks our brains into thinking that the lunar disk is larger while in the presence of foreground objects compared to when it is overhead.

It'll make for a breathtaking photo opportunity, which you can capitalize on with our beginner's guide to imaging the full moon, along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for capturing the night sky.

Editor's Note: If you take a photo of the November full moon and would like to share it with Space.com's readers, then please send your photos and comments, along with your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

Has AI just cracked Internet encryption? Rumoured ‘bombshell’ stuns scientists

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Public-key cryptography helps to secure everything from online banking and private messages to sensitive government communications.Credit: Peshkov/Getty.
  • Recent findings suggest that artificial-intelligence agents have already begun to wreak havoc by hacking into servers around the world, either spontaneously or directed by humans.
  • Several computer scientists have suggested on social media that the leading AI laboratories — companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic, both in San Francisco, California — have discovered algorithms that could derail the security of Internet communications.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Public-key cryptography helps to secure everything from online banking and private messages to sensitive government communications.Credit: Peshkov/Getty.

Recent findings suggest that artificial-intelligence agents have already begun to wreak havoc by hacking into servers around the world, either spontaneously or directed by humans. Now, a threat is emerging that is on a whole other scale.

Several computer scientists have suggested on social media that the leading AI laboratories — companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic, both in San Francisco, California — have discovered algorithms that could derail the security of Internet communications.

‘If we can solve Riemann, what can’t we do?’: mathematicians shocked and excited by AI breakthroughs.

‘If we can solve Riemann, what can’t we do?’: mathematicians shocked and excited by AI breakthroughs.

“I’m virtually certain, from multiple reliable sources, that the AI labs are now sitting on one or more bombshells,” computer scientist Scott Aaronson wrote yesterday on his blog. The details are still hazy, added Aaronson, who is at the University of Texas at Austin. “Until I either see details or hear directly from someone at a lab, I feel much, much less confident about the specific nature of those bombshells.”.

The algorithms are rumoured to target the information-scrambling system known as RSA, which relies on the mathematics of prime numbers, as well as more-advanced technologies.

While the rumours could not be confirmed, other breakthroughs revealed by the AI companies this week make researchers cautiously optimistic that the mathematics of encryption could eventually come to help.

Nature examines the threat, and what can be done about it.

Several researchers say they have heard that some of the leading AI laboratories have discovered algorithms capable of breaking public-key cryptography in ‘polynomial time’ (or ‘P’ in computer-science shorthand).

Recent findings suggest that public-key cryptography helps to secure everything from banking apps to Internet browsers. It relies on mathematical problems that are considered practically impossible for computers to solve within a reasonable amount of time.

According to recent reports, an algorithm that could solve these problems in polynomial time would change that. It means the time needed to solve a problem would increase relatively slowly as the problem gets larger. For example, a password of length n could be broken in a number of steps proportional to the square or cube of its size (n² or n³).

The race to save the Internet from quantum hackers.

The race to save the Internet from quantum hackers.

Sources indicate that theoretical computer scientists tend to think of P problems as relatively easy to solve, especially compared with problems that require exponential time, where the number of steps might grow as 2n, for example. As n gets larger — or a password gets longer — the time required by an exponential algorithm promptly exceeds that of any polynomial one.

In practical terms, an algorithm that could break public-key cryptography in polynomial time could undermine much of the security on which the Internet relies.

It depends on which encryption systems they could crack, and how efficiently they could do so.

Recent findings suggest that one of the most ubiquitous techniques for establishing public keys is to multiply two large prime numbers. This technique, called RSA, was long believed to be secure because ‘cracking the code’ requires factoring that product back into the original primes, a much slower process (at least, without a powerful quantum computer, which does not yet exist). One of the rumours now circulating is that the AI labs have found an algorithm that can do this.

Recent findings suggest that but even though a polynomial-time algorithm could be very powerful on paper, it could still be impossible to use except for the shortest passwords. An algorithm requiring n10000steps, for example, be very impractical to apply.

According to recent reports, however, proving that a problem is in ‘P’, even if the polynomial-time solution is practically useless, has usually been followed by improvements that have eventually led to efficient solutions. “The matter is that the idea that [the problem] was hard — because of needing exponential time — is dead,” Aaronson tells Nature.

Not necessarily. This type of worst-case scenario hinges on a long-standing open question known as ‘P = NP’: could every problem whose solution can be checked in polynomial time also be solved in polynomial time? If so, problems that underpin essentially all public-key cryptography could become much easier to crack.

Quantum-computing pioneer warns of complacency over Internet security.

Quantum-computing pioneer warns of complacency over Internet security.

In a recent development, but most researchers think that this is unlikely. In fact, some recent AI-aided results have made them cautiously optimistic. Earlier this week, both Anthropic and OpenAI revealed results in theoretical computer science that suggest that many similar problems could be hard to solve. Before the recent explosion in AI-aided maths, each of those advances would have been hailed as the computer-science breakthrough of the decade, Aaronson states.

Ryan Williams, a computer scientist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge, agrees. “I am definitely blown away by the latest developments.” One especially interesting result, he claims, indicates that for a ubiquitous type of computation called matrix multiplication, the exponent in a polynomial-time algorithm cannot be too small. “Underneath the hood, it seems to provide a brand-new framework for proving limitations on efficient computation,” says Williams.

Hearts' European hopes hang by a thread but Vrancken proud

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (727 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hearts' hopes of a memorable draw with Monaco were dashed in the 94th minute.
  • There was a bittersweet feeling at Tynecastle after Folarin Balogun's 94th-minute winner preserved Monaco's perfect Conference League record and condemned Hearts to a third defeat from four.
  • Wouter Vrancken's side had gone toe-to-toe with one of the best teams in the tournament, scored two glorious goals, but ultimately came away with nothing for their efforts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hearts' hopes of a memorable draw with Monaco were dashed in the 94th minute.

There was a bittersweet feeling at Tynecastle after Folarin Balogun's 94th-minute winner preserved Monaco's perfect Conference League record and condemned Hearts to a third defeat from four.

Wouter Vrancken's side had gone toe-to-toe with one of the best teams in the tournament, scored two glorious goals, but ultimately came away with nothing for their efforts.

Now they have little to no margin for error in their two remaining league phase matches.

They will likely have to beat both Borac Banja Luka of Bosnia and Cyprus' Pafos to reach the knockout stages, but if they perform as they did against Monaco, they will give themselves a fighting chance.

Hearts have garnered a reputation as entertainers under Vrancken - scoring a raft of goals while being porous at the back.

Sources indicate that this game was their season in microcosm. The goals - scored by Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota - were things of beauty, picture-perfect strikes worthy of any stage.

But as thrilling as Hearts were in attack, they were as baffling at the back.

Jamie McCart unnecessarily tripped Matthis Abline, allowing Balogun to score from the penalty spot and Monaco's second came from Altena giving the ball away.

"It's Gladiators - are we not entertained? It's sensational," stated Hearts legend John Robertson at half-time, with the game finely poised at 2-2.

Monaco strike in 94th minute to break Hearts in five-goal epic.

Latest Hearts news, analysis and fan views.

Both teams had chances to win it in the second half, but it was Monaco who took theirs in the final stages. Mamadou Coulibaly was afforded too much space and he slipped Balogun through to beat Beau Reus.

"It's a lack of nous and a little bit of naivety," former Hearts midfielder Michael Stewart stated on TNT Sports. "McCart backs off and allows the ball to be played into Balogun's feet.".

Despite the frustrating nature of the late concession, Vrancken's overwhelming emotion was of pride.

"I'm very disappointed with how we give the goal away at the end," he mentioned.

"The biggest thing is the pride for the performance today. Against a side of Monaco's [quality] - we're still missing nine players through injury - this performance was really pleasing.".

Before the recent international break, Hearts were beaten 3-1 by Swiss outfit Thun, before a shock 5-2 home defeat by high-flying Falkirk in the Scottish Premiership.

However, they bounced back with a ruthless 8-0 win at Dundee on Saturday and carried that confidence into this game against a team with a far bigger budget.

"You saw that the confidence was there from the weekend and there was conviction around their box," Vrancken added. "It will not work every time, but the conviction and energy was there again.

"Our team kept their heads in the game and kept going for it, not being pleased with 2-2. Really pleased with what I saw.".

Aside from his dismay at Balogun's winner and how it came about, Vrancken's main gripe was with the officials.

He felt there was a foul on Kerjota in the build-up to Monaco's second goal and was bemused at the fact neither Takumi Minamino and Denis Zakaria were sent off.

Minamino - already on a yellow card - wiped out Sabri Guendouz on the edge of the Monaco box, but got away with a warning. And VAR opted not to intervene after Zakaria went over the top of the ball and caught Pierre Landry Kabore on the shin.

"The second goal, they pulled Sabah [Kerjota] and he can't do his defensive work," Vrancken said.

"It was not the only refereeing decision that was interesting tonight. I don't know how it's possible not to give a red card for the tackle on [Pierre Landry Kabore]. It's clearly above the ankle, so it's always a red card.

"And why didn't Minamino get a second yellow before half-time? He prevents a shot from Sabri at the edge of the box.

Industry observers note that "The explanation of the fourth official was even more crazy - he explained it could be for his first yellow card, but not for his second yellow. It was clearly a yellow card and then we were against 10 in the second half.".

Vrancken on Hearts' narrow Monaco defeat.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brad Friedel made 450 Premier League appearances during a long and distinguished career at the top level – now he’s embarking upon a new challenge in League Two.

Following retirement in 2015, Friedel later had spells managing the USA under 19s side and MLS club Fresh England Revolution, before a brief stint as an advisor at Besiktas in Turkey.

Earlier this month, he became the fresh sporting director at Shrewsbury Town, after being part of a US consortium that completed a takeover of the club.

Shrewsbury have endured tough times in recent seasons as they waited for upcoming investment, suffering relegation from League One in 2024, then finishing 19th in the fourth tier last term.

They sit mid-table in League Two this season, though, and had previously spent a decade in the third tier.

Scott Davidson's American-based consortium Biscayne ST LLC have now bought the club, with Friedel moving to the area to take a hands-on role as sporting director.

Speaking to FourFourTwo in his new role, he explained that he’s relishing the challenge and that Shrewsbury were very carefully chosen from a list of possible options.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

“We had a long look at clubs, and we had a long list of criteria for clubs,” he said, speaking in association with 711 Sports.

“We looked in the United Kingdom, we looked in various places throughout Europe and when all was mentioned and done, it was Shrewsbury Town that ticked the boxes for us.

“We feel that there’s just an incredible upside and potential in the town and at the club, and we feel we’ve created a very good board that can help the community, as well as the team on the pitch.

“We feel there are areas for improvement at the club, but we also feel there’s a very strong base that was previously built at the club, so it was a long list of reasons why it made sense for us.”.

There will be more from Friedel about Shrewsbury and his career in football in FourFourTwo soon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Chelsea slumped to a third successive Premier League defeat as they went down 3-2 at Nottingham Forest to mount the pressure on boss Xabi Alonso.

The London club were second-best to Forest, who won it through Igor Jesus’ brilliant opener and a Morgan Gibbs-White double after the break.

Emmanuel Emegha scored twice to give the scoreline a different complexion, but that does not mask the overall poor performance.

The latest loss comes after last weekend’s alarming 4-1 defeat to Leeds and Alonso has clear issues to address as they slide down the table.

One of them is Wesley Fofana after the Frenchman was booed and jeered by his own fans after an unauthorised YouTube interview where he appeared to joke about the club’s Carabao Cup exit.

Forest claimed back-to-back home wins after beating Manchester City last time out at the City Ground and this performance was an indication that they are moving in the right direction under Oliver Glasner.

Sources indicate that alonso opted to change his defence after last week’s debacle against Leeds, dropping Levi Colwill and replacing him in the back four with midfielder Moises Caicedo. The Spaniard did stick with under-fire Fofana, who was booed from the off.

Both men came under early pressure as Forest began well. Liam Delap, desperate to score against the club where his career stalled last season, had a snap-shot in the first minute, but Emiliano Martinez was not troubled.

But the Argentina goalkeeper could do nothing about a sublime Forest opener in the fifth minute. Daniel Munoz drilled in a cross from that right that Jesus sent into the top corner with an acrobatic volley. It was a fine piece of athleticism, even if contact did come off the shin.

That was the only real moment of quality in a first half where Forest were the better side. Alonso’s men had nothing going forward and failed to muster a shot on target.

According to recent reports, things did not improve after the break as Fofana’s night got worse. He lost out on a routine challenge to Delap, who burst clear into the box and was felled by the Frenchman.

Referee Andy Madley pointed to the spot and Gibbs-White stepped up and sent Martinez the wrong way.

But Chelsea got themselves back into it three minutes later, with their first shot on target, and they needed plenty of luck.

Pedro Neto’s shot hit Jair Cunha and it fell kindly into the path of half-time substitute Emegha, who rifled into the bottom corner.

Fofana was then hooked as he was put out of his mercy, but Chelsea still looked vulnerable.

James McAtee should have done better with his shot after a fine pass by Gibbs-White, while Murillo’s thumping volley from distance brought a good save by Martinez.

It has been revealed that forest restored their two-goal cushion in the 72nd minute as they scored an excellent third. Xaver Schlager picked up a loose ball, made space with a fine first touch and then found Gibbs-White with an incisive pass, which the England international coolly clipped home.

They appeared to be seeing the match out with ease, but that changed in the 89th minute as Chelsea scored out of nothing.

Neto’s cross found Emegha who headed home to set up a grandstand finish, but Forest held on for a deserved three points.

According to recent reports, november's full moon rises tonight (Nov. 24)! You can see live telescopic views of the "Beaver supermoon" courtesy of the Virtual Telescope Project (VTP).

The free YouTube livestream begins at 10:30 a.m. EST (1530 GMT) and will feature live views of the moon captured by a suite of robotic telescopes in Manciano, Italy, weather permitting.

Today's stream features expert commentary from VTP founder Gianluca Masi, along with photos of previous full moons shining above historic landmarks in the heart of Rome.

November's full moon is often called the Beaver Moon because it rises around the time the industrious animals are hard at work building dams and preparing for the winter months, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac.

It is also set to be a spectacular supermoon, which reaches peak illumination while within 90% of perigee — the closest point to Earth in the moon's 27-day elliptical orbit.

You might like: November full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Beaver Moon.

Supermoons can be up to 13% larger and 30% brighter than the smallest full moon of the year, which occurred in May earlier this year as the natural satellite shone opposite the sun in Earth's sky while close to apogee, when it is farthest from our planet.

US and UK to host Women's World Cups in 2031 and 2035

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (370 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • FIFA have confirmed the hosts for the 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cup.
  • Recent findings suggest that the United States, along with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, made an uncontested bid to host in 2031.
  • Recent findings suggest that FIFA's revenue for the 2026 men's World Cup was around $15 billion (€13.7 billion), and it's clear that US Soccer feels that hosting the women's tournament is the next move forward.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

FIFA have confirmed the hosts for the 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cup.

Recent findings suggest that the United States, along with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, made an uncontested bid to host in 2031. It will be the first tournament to feature 48 teams — as is the case with the men. The US has hosted the event twice before, in 2003 and 1999, and is also the most successful country in its history, having won it four times.

Recent findings suggest that FIFA's revenue for the 2026 men's World Cup was around $15 billion (€13.7 billion), and it's clear that US Soccer feels that hosting the women's tournament is the next move forward. With the women's domestic league (NWSL) considered the strongest in the world and the US national team so dominant, securing the tournament in 2031 is a further sign of the US' committment to women's football.

"We expect and blueprint for the 2031 Women’s World Cup to be the largest women’s sporting event in history," Emily Cosler, US Soccer’s vice-president of strategy told The Guardian.

The 2035 tournament was also awarded to the sole bidders, England, Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales. This sees the World Cup return to the United Kingdom for the first time since 1966, the only time England's men's team won the competition. The women lost the 2023 final to Spain. It also means that the UK will host two major tournaments in relatively quick succession, with the men's 2028 European Championships also set to be held in England, Scotland and Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham noted the tournament would bring "visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.".

It has been revealed that given that FIFA President Gianni Infantino had revealed last year that both bids were unchallenged, this news comes as little surprise. Nevertheless, with the hosts now official, a 48-team tournament marks a remarkable advance for the women's game. The 2011 World Cup in Germany had just 16 teams.

The next World Cup will be in Brazil in 2027, running from June 24 to July 25. . Eighteen of the 32 teams have already secured qualification, including Germany.

Lammens - the Man Utd goalkeeper under scrutiny like never before
