According to recent reports, TL;DR: The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free when you switch to T-Mobile and bring your number on a qualifying T-Mix plan. This Black Friday deal is only available for a limited time.

Sources indicate that black Friday deals are coming in hot and heavy. We're inundated with fresh price drops on laptops, headphones, fitness trackers, and everything in between. And yes, we're seeing a huge number of price drops on Apple.

Wading through the deals on iPads, MacBooks, and AirPods, it's tough to ignore T-Mobile's massive sale on iPhones. If you've been waiting until now to upgrade, you're in luck: For limited-time, the Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free at T-Mobile. Yes, you read that right.

Sources indicate that T-Mobile keeps things surprisingly flexible when it comes to qualifying for this Black Friday deal. You can port your existing phone number from an eligible rival carrier to a qualifying T-Mix initiative, and T-Mobile covers the full cost of the phone. Alternatively, existing customers can trade in an eligible phone in any condition on a qualifying T-Mix plan.

Industry observers note that T-Mobile distributes the full discount as 36 monthly bill credits. If you leave T-Mobile or cancel your line before that three-year payment strategy ends, the credits stop immediately, and you will owe the remaining balance on the device.

In a recent development, you are also still required to pay local sales tax on the phone's full $1,199 retail value upfront, plus T-Mobile's standard $35 device connection fee per line at checkout. Unfortunately, you can't escape those upfront charges.

Score the Apple iPhone 18 Pro for free with T-Mobile over Black Friday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the November full moon rose to put on a spectacular natural light show on Nov.
  • Sources indicate that each monthly full moon has its own set of informal names, often bestowed to reflect events occurring in the world at the time of their rising.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the November full moon rose to put on a spectacular natural light show on Nov. 24 and we've got the photos to prove it! Read on to see our favorite shots of the "Beaver Moon" captured from around the world.

Sources indicate that each monthly full moon has its own set of informal names, often bestowed to reflect events occurring in the world at the time of their rising. The November moon is often known as the Beaver Moon, a name associated with the time of year when beavers prepare for winter and when trappers historically set beaver traps before waterways froze.

November's full moon served as the opening salvo in a series of four dazzling supermoons, which turn full around the time that the natural satellite passes closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit.

That added proximity can make it appear noticeably brighter and larger than the smallest full moon of the year, setting the stage for an incredible photo shoot as the lunar disk climbed high into the autumn sky.

Our first shot of the moon was captured by photographer Pongmanat Tasiri as the moon rose over the roof of the Wat Phra That Doi Suthep Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, as a stunning array of craters and lunar seas scar the Beaver Moon's surface.

Meanwhile, Gary Hershorn snapped a gorgeous shot of the full yellow moon rising over the Chrysler Building in Fresh York, with the Empire State Building and myriad other skyscrapers dominating the skyline.

Hershorn also managed to line up a colorful shot of the lunar disk glowing between the concrete canyon of Fresh York's iconic 42nd Street just before moonset on the morning of Nov. 24, mere hours before the moon turned full.

NASA astronaut Anil Menon snapped a series of stunning photos from the International Space Station on Nov. 24, November full moon slipped out of view below Earth's horizon, while being gradually deformed by the warping effect of our planet's atmosphere. "Moonset today from space station - no edits to these photos from 400mm lens," Menon wrote in a post on X.

Heading back down to Earth Salih Zeki Fazlioglu took a colorful photo of the Beaver moon illuminating a thin veil of clouds above Istanbul, Turkiye, as reflected sunlight competed with the artificial glow of the city below for the viewer's attention.

According to recent reports, this shot of the lunar disk looming over the Old Post Office Pavillion in Washington D.C. was captured by David Ake, with the pink sky complementing the orange and red leaves of autumn.

It has been revealed that our next photo was captured by Space.com's Skywatching Editor Daisy Dobrijevic using a Sony A7IV with a Tamron 50-400mm lens as the moon shone in the skies over the city of Nottingham in the U.K. on Nov. 23.

According to recent reports, "Having seen the rather disappointing weather forecast for the night of the full moon, I decided to head out a day early and capture the almost-full Beaver Moon instead," explained Dobrijevic. "It hadn’t quite risen above the rooftops of the houses opposite me, so I took a peek down the alleyway and, sure enough, there it was, nestled between two houses, giving me just enough of a clear view to capture this close-up.".

This striking image of the full moon rising above the Toronto skyline was snapped by Mert Alper Dervis as a flock of birds skimmed through the foreground. The outline of the lunar disk appears subtly warped and squashed by atmospheric refraction, as its reflected light passes through pockets of air with differing densities and temperatures.

According to recent reports, allen Berman sent in a breathtaking photo of the full moon hanging low over the Los Angeles skyline on the night of Nov. 24.

"Finding the right spot for tonight’s full moon over downtown Los Angeles was a bit tricky," Berman told Space.com. "We wound up on a neighbor’s front lawn in the Baldwin Hills section of town. The owner was a bit surprised to see photographers there. But he was cool. The conditions were perfect with thin clouds over the distant mountains that made for a magical image.".

In a recent development, moving from the modern to the old, photographer Robert Nemeti took a moody shot of the full Beaver Moon climbing skyward above the medieval Boldogkő Castle in Hungary at moonrise on Nov. 24. How many full moons must that old building have seen?

Wang Zhao snapped a very different view from Beijing, China, on that same night by using a powerful telephoto lens to capture a passenger jet as it streaked across the lunar disk, leaving dense contrails in its wake.

It has been revealed that that Beaver Moon was captured shining between the minarets of the Imam Ali Shrine in the city of Najaf, Iraq, by Karar Essa. The 53-mile-wide (85-kilometer) Tycho Crater can be seen as a distinctive bright feature below the lunar equator, close to the dark expanse of Mare Nubium.

Aris Oikonomou snapped a striking photo of the Beaver Moon shining above the Parthenon in Athens, Greece, just as night began to set in over the Acropolis.

Feeling inspired to capture your own supermoon photos? Then be sure to read our guide to photographing the moon and browse our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography because you don't have long to wait!

It has been revealed that the final supermoon of 2026 rises in just a few short weeks on Dec. 23 and it just so happens to be the closest full moon of the year, passing just 221,668 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth at the point of maximum illumination.

So no excuses! We'd love to see your photo in our inbox next month.

#163758. Industry News: How cautious investors are struggling to avoid the AI bubble

Industry News: How cautious investors are struggling to avoid the AI bubble

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1069 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index roared back to life this week after a worrying sell-off recently that saw huge falls in technology and artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks.
  • After suffering its worst week since the pandemic crash of March 2020, the Nasdaq opened Monday (November 23) nearly 1,700 points, or 7%, higher.
  • The AI trade received a further boost after Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang on Monday, just 11 days after he was forced to resign amid a scandal involving extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index roared back to life this week after a worrying sell-off recently that saw huge falls in technology and artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks.

After suffering its worst week since the pandemic crash of March 2020, the Nasdaq opened Monday (November 23) nearly 1,700 points, or 7%, higher.

The AI trade received a further boost after Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang on Monday, just 11 days after he was forced to resign amid a scandal involving extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

The chipmaker's stock rose more than 30% on the news, opening at nearly $170 (€155.5) per share and recovering most of the losses since last month, when the affair was first reported.

The surge helped propel US stock indices to their best day since last year. But in premarket trading on Tuesday, Nvidia fell about 5%, underscoring the volatility of the market and the risks facing the AI sector and the broader tech industry.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The recent volatility around AI, memory chips and other technology stocks has unnerved even the most experienced and bullish investors.

Yet, those seeking a haven away from the United States stock market, which has enjoyed the majority of the AI hype — along with Taiwan and South Korea — are increasingly finding few places to shelter.

In a recent development, economists warn that this is partly due to the way index funds, including exchange-traded funds (ETFs), work. These funds hold the pensions and other savings of hundreds of millions of passive investors.

These indices have become increasingly exposed to the AI boom.

In a recent development, most flagship index funds are keen to ride winners, so they automatically buy stocks according to a company's market value. The bigger a company grows, the more of it they hold.

The values of Nvidia, Microsoft, Apple, Alphabet and other US technology giants have benefited from this effect, with many soaring after ChatGPT was first released in late 2022.

The US also has an outsized position in funds that track the global economy. Nine of the top 10 holdings of the MSCI All Country World Index (ACWI), an index of more than 2,400 firms across 47 developed and emerging markets, are US Major Tech names.

The other is TSMC, a Taiwanese chipmaker that produces 90% of the high-end AI semiconductors.

Together, these 10 holdings make up nearly a quarter of the index.

Although it's a global index, nearly two-thirds of MSCI ACWI's value is in US-listed companies, even though they make up only around a fifth of its firms.

"A well-diversified portfolio should ... reasonably represent the entire global economy," Gerd Kommer, founder of the Munich-based asset manager Gerd Kommer Invest, told DW.

"That's not the case if 70% of the portfolio is concentrated in just one country — the US. The global economy is more resilient than any national economy.".

Kommer, who is known as Germany's "ETF pope," said investors need exposure to all economic sectors and that no single sector should make up more than a quarter of a portfolio.

Yet, even if investors want to avoid US-dominated World funds altogether, the AI trade still overshadows several other top index funds.

In MSCI's Emerging Market index, for example, the top 10 make up 37.5% of its value and TSMC alone accounts for almost 16%. Tech, chip and internet firms make up eight of the largest holdings, alongside two banks — one Chinese, one Indian.

That matters, according to Dimitri Vayanos, a finance professor at the London School of Economics who studies how passive investing pushes up the prices of the biggest firms.

"My model suggests that the effects of flows into index funds are larger when the large stocks happen to be in the same industry," Vayanos told DW.

When some investors get over-optimistic about a manufacturer and push the stock price up, index funds add to that price pressure.

According to recent reports, professional investors then often bet against overpriced stocks, a practice known as "shorting," which helps pull prices back down. But that's far riskier with, say, a tech giant than with a small firm.

"Being short 1% of SpaceX involves much more risk than being short 1% of a small tech giant," said Vayanos.

The problem gets worse when the biggest firms are all in the same sector, as they are now. As short-sellers hold back, the biggest stocks climb further, creating what he calls an "amplification-overpricing spiral.".

To cut exposure to AI-related stocks, investors may have to turn to developed market funds outside the US and Southeast Asia. These funds have offered lower returns over the past decade.

In the MSCI Europe, Australasia and Far East (EAFE) index fund, the top 10 holdings make up about 14.5% of the index, about 40% lower than the all-country world index.

EAFE's major holdings include healthcare giant Roche, oil major Shell, HSBC bank and Nestle — the world's largest food and beverage tech giant.

However, its biggest holding, ASML, is still very much part of the AI trade. The Dutch tech firm sells the equipment that firms such as TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SK Hynix and Micron need to make their chips.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

If Monday's rebound in the AI trade is sustained, stock prices may move sharply higher over the next few months. Yet if history is a guide, the bubble will eventually burst, leaving both institutional and passive investors nursing heavy losses.

Kommer warned that if the AI bubble bursts, "in all likelihood it will drag down the global stock market," though the damage would be most severe in tech and AI stocks.

Those hit hardest would be retail investors "with heavy portfolio weights in tech and AI stocks," he mentioned, including "a lot of people who have bought individual AI-related stocks on top of their equity ETFs.".

LSE's Vayanos thinks it is still "certainly safer to hold an ETF than to hold individual stocks.".

But as index providers add mega-IPOs such as SpaceX and Claude-maker Anthropic to benchmarks within weeks of their debut, and money continues to pour into passive funds, he warned that "the conditions are present for the effects of our theory to be even stronger.".

Industry News: What makes or breaks a high press?

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1773 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz spearhead Liverpool's press under Andoni Iraola.
  • A good high press has been the basis for some of the most successful sides in modern football but a well-oiled pressing machine has many moving parts - all requiring close attention.
  • When an out-of-possession plan is implemented poorly, entire seasons can fall apart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz spearhead Liverpool's press under Andoni Iraola.

A good high press has been the basis for some of the most successful sides in modern football but a well-oiled pressing machine has many moving parts - all requiring close attention.

When an out-of-possession plan is implemented poorly, entire seasons can fall apart.

In a recent development, so, what determines whether a press works or fails? And how are the always-adapting Premier League teams exploiting high presses this season?

In a recent development, when a team decides to press, they must first establish their intention. This informs how the players act.

Speaking to DAZN Portugal, Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler was asked about whether a good press relied more on physicality or courage.

"A really good question," he began.

It has been revealed that "When you want to press high you need the courage and mindset to do it. Our mindset is we press to score, we don't just press to win the ball back.".

In coaching, clarity is key - particularly when it comes to creating alignment in the squad and Hurzeler is deliberate in simplifying big ideas when delivering messages to his players, a skill he practised as a radio pundit during the World Cup.

"[Punditry] helps you as a coach in that you have to summarise things in a short and easy way so that everyone understands," he said. "Football might get more complex but simplicity counts.".

Hurzeler's "pressing to score" is a phrase that communicates many ideas in a memorable three words: intensity, being proactive, and immediate forward-thinking on winning the ball.

It also frames pressing in a way that makes it easy for attackers to buy into, in the form of goals.

"You want commitment from everyone on the pitch," Hurzeler explained.

"If just one has doubts, the whole press is gone.".

The Red Bull school of coaching uses a similarly succinct phrase - "the last step" to address these ideas around intention, collectiveness and aggression.

Summarised by Tactx, whose coaches have worked under the Red Bull model, the last step refers to "players [being] coached to attack through the opponent, using the final step to lunge aggressively at the ball".

"This action commits the defender fully and is often the decisive moment that allows possession to be won.".

Pressing to engage rather than just to close distances ensures the team in possession aren't given the time or space to play through otherwise half-hearted pressure.

Applying team-wide pressure, Newcastle make a strong tackle and win the ball.

This forces a turnover that puts Newcastle in a favourable attacking position.

When discussing how good or bad a team is at pressing, how much they run is often brought up. But the distance a team covers fails to paint the full picture when it comes to the effectiveness of a team's pressing strategy.

Liverpool's current boss Andoni Iraola was asked about how he interpreted physical data last year.

"It's not 'we run a lot, so we are good,' no," he said. "The high-speed running, the sprint speeds [matter for us] - not total distance covered.

"[Some] teams that do not run a lot get very good results because they have [their] way of playing.".

Sprints matter more than distance covered for Iraola's side, who have clear ideas of how to press, looking to win the ball back through a sudden and intense pressure from familiar positions they are well prepared for.

If the conditions to implement this press aren't on, the wingers can be seen dropping off, forming a more compact defensive shape with the likes of Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz defending in a front two for longer periods of the match.

It's smart. Liverpool look to maximise the effectiveness of when they do press, with full commitment expected in each sprint, with players conserving their energy in moments a press is less likely to succeed.

With pressing being a front-footed idea, coaches may throw caution to the wind but this can leave them exposed in ways teams have become better at exploiting.

Hurzeler touched on the need for balance when pressing.

"I always say in certain moments you need to have the courage to take risk but you need to have the discipline to control the risk," he remarked.

For Brighton, this looks like certain players abandoning man-to-man marking when their respective attacker attempts to drag them into awkward positions.

Instead, Brighton will protect the centre of the pitch on top of their man-to-man principles which helps them stay compact.

In yellow, we can see the man-oriented defence of Brighton against Arsenal. The players highlighted in white are taking a more central position designed to protect dangerous areas of the pitch. This is an example of how impressive coaches are combining man-to-man pressing with zonal ideas.

Sources indicate that when the defending side aren't compact, spaces exist for the attacking side to target. When players step up to press, these gaps can arise in between the lines.

Again, Brighton manage to plug these gaps well by pressing hard, reducing the time opponents have to play passes into midfield, while also encouraging players to make vertical jumps up the pitch, covering players left by teammates who have pressed higher up the pitch.

As Declan Rice passes the ball backwards, Brighton's players press forward, locking on to the player in front of them.

Chema Andres recognises that Bruno Guimaraes has been left unmarked in midfield so makes a vertical jump, closing him down, and ensuring Brighton remain compact.

When teams lack vertical compactness - not pressing with enough intensity and without making the necessary steps up the pitch - the space left in midfield has been exploited by clever sides, such as Leeds.

In their 4-1 loss to Daniel Farke's men, Chelsea looked to press high, with attackers and midfielders running up the pitch to apply pressure.

But when the ball went back the other way, these same players struggled.

In a recent development, the idea behind playing over a team's press isn't always to make the ball stick at the feet of a target man, although this helps. Instead space is found in the gaps between the pressing side's lines.

Recognising when teammates are likely to win headers or clip the ball forwards, midfielders are able to turn and run in the direction the ball is heading in, positioned ready to win second balls in numbers.

By comparison, the pressing side's midfielders, having to apply forward pressure before turning around to track back are often slower to contest second balls.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea play a long goal-kick towards Leeds' back line. This forward pass brings with it the forward pressure of Chelsea's attackers and midfielders. The Leeds' defender heads it back, against the direction of Chelsea's press.

According to recent reports, leeds' midfielders have oriented themselves well to form a net around where the ball may drop. The Chelsea midfielders and attackers, starting from further away and having to turn around, aren't well placed to contest for the loose ball.

According to recent reports, the same ideas are seen again. The Leeds' midfielder, under insufficient pressure, is able to play the ball forward promptly. This catches Chelsea's midfield line high up the pitch. Chelsea's Romeo Lavia has to turn before he can get back into position whilst Leeds attacking midfielders are closer to the ball, facing forwards.

This allows Leeds to exploit the space between Chelsea's lines.

By this point, it will be clear that pressing is influenced by countless variables but it is worth highlighting one final factor; teams need solutions when pressing with one fewer player than the attacking side.

This most obviously happens when the opposition goalkeeper is involved in build-up play.

Here, the team in possession have 11 options against the 10 pressing players.

Obvious solutions come in the form one of the forward attackers pressing a centre-back at an angle which usually forces them to pass it back to the goalkeeper.

At that point, the same pressing player will continue his run, now pressing the keeper.

By curving their run and pressing at an angle, the idea is that the keeper will struggle to pass it back to the now unmarked centre-back.

This is generally true but again, good teams have found smart solutions to access this player.

Industry observers note that charalampos Kostoulas first presses Gabriel Magalhaes, who passes the ball to his keeper, David Raya. Kostoulas then curves his run, blocking off Raya's pass back to Gabriel.

One solution comes when the keeper passes the ball into a central player who then bounces the pass into the unmarked centre-back. This comes with risk given that the central player is usually marked. But sudden darts towards the ball can give them the time and space to play the bounce pass required.

Under some pressure, Rice darts towards the ball, gaining some separation from his marker. He gestures for the ball knowing he can play a first time pass to Gabriel who is unmarked.

In a recent development, what happens instead is Raya, under immense pressure, defaults to playing long. His pass ends up out of play.

A riskier but more impressive solution is when the keeper is willing and able to avoid the opponents attempt to force him in one direction, instead playing the ball back the other way themselves.

Queens Park Rangers' Pierce Charles, on loan from Manchester City, has done this better than most in world football, and his quality was clearest against Swansea's excellent press.

By playing against the direction of Swansea's press, to his unmarked teammate, he was able to immediately disorganise their press.

QPR's right-sided defender passes the ball back to Charles. The Swansea striker, first pressing the defender, angles his body to discourage Charles from playing back to the unmarked player. He closes Charles down as he does this.

Swansea's press is designed to force Charles to his left but he bravely plays back the other way.

By finding the unmarked man on the other side in space, Swansea have to reorganise their defensive shape.

Changes in how a team presses force teams to innovate their build-up play which in turn force teams to innovate in how they press. It's a cycle that spins at a blistering pace, especially in the Premier League.

Given the detailed analysis and constant adaptation, teams and coaches in 2026 can ill-afford to rest on their laurels.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It was just six months ago that Graham Potter was deemed the man to usher in a fresh, exciting era at Chelsea.

The club’s fresh ownership group, led by American businessman Todd Boehly, had enticed Potter away from Brighton with the promise of managing one of the most lucrative teams in world soccer.

More than $600 million was spent on bringing big-name players to the club and Potter, one of the most exciting young managers in the Premier League, was to mold them into a winning machine.

Industry observers note that chelsea has spent over $600 million on new signings. Here's why that's significant.

But, on Sunday, the club announced that it had sacked its manager after an underwhelming spell in charge.

Potter managed to win just 10 of the 28 league matches this season and leaves the team 11th in the Premier League table.

In recent weeks, players had looked a shadow of their former selves and many fans had lost confidence that Potter’s proposal for the club could ever work.

Eventually, after previously sticking by its manager, Blues ownership agreed.

“On behalf of everyone at the club, we want to thank Graham sincerely for his contribution to Chelsea,” the club’s co-owners Todd Boehly and Behdad Eghbali said in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that “We have the highest degree of respect for Graham as a coach and as a person. He has always conducted himself with professionalism and integrity and we are all disappointed in this outcome.”.

In his previous role as Brighton manager, Potter was given time to stamp his identity on the squad.

The club was punching above its weight financially and, as a result, carefully selected new signings which would compliment Potter’s style of play.

The approach paid off as the team became an established Premier League outfit which has gone on to greater things this season – the Seagulls at the moment sit sixth in the league and in the UEFA Conference League qualification spot.

At Chelsea, it seemed the complete opposite.

As was the case under previous owner Roman Abramovich, the club expected instant results and used its financial weight to sign a number of high-profile names, including the likes of Enzo Fernández and Mykhailo Mudryk.

Despite his impressive CV, Potter had never managed superstars and suddenly found himself in a changing room with multiple.

The scatter gun approach to recruitment also left the team lacking balance and organization with Potter failing to get a tune out of a team busting with talent.

In truth, many had raised an eyebrow when Potter, inexperienced at the very top level, was chosen to replace Thomas Tuchel as manager.

Despite falling out of favor with fans by the end of his tenure, Tuchel had guided Chelsea to the Champions League title in 2021 and is still considered by many as one of the best coaches in the world.

The German has gone on to sign with Bavarian giant Bayern Munich through the 2024/25 season and recently told reporters he needed “quite a bit of time to distance himself from Chelsea” because leaving the club had hurt him.

Bayern Munich sacks manager Julian Nagelsmann, appoints Thomas Tuchel.

“Todd [Boehly] noted he would be different to Roman [Abramovich],” former Liverpool player and current pundit Jamie Carragher wrote on Twitter.

According to recent reports, “I feel for Graham Potter, but it was inevitable. You don’t change Tuchel for Potter. Ridiculous decision to start with.”.

With 10 games left in the league and a Champions League quarterfinal against Real Madrid on the horizon, Chelsea still has plenty to play for.

Assistant coach Bruno Saltor will take over on an interim basis, but Boehly and his team must now look for a long-term replacement capable – and willing – to bring order to Chelsea’s chaos.

Potter’s sacking is yet another sign of just how transient managers can be in the top-flight of English football, especially when results aren’t instantaneous.

There has now been a record 12 sackings in the Premier League so far this season, with Potter leaving his position the same day Leicester boss Brendan Rodgers was sacked from his.

The previous record was 10 manager changes in a single season, set in four other campaigns, most recently in 2017/18.

Winger has not played for the USMNT since the World Cup and believes good club form is his route back into the squad.

Industry observers note that this was the USMNT’s summer. By extension, it was also that of the 26 players selected by Mauricio Pochettino to represent the nation at a home World Cup. It didn’t live up to expectations for all of them, and certainly not for Timothy Weah. “Obviously this summer wasn’t the best for me,” he says.

It has been revealed that weah was one of eight players in the squad to have started all four of the US’s matches in Qatar in 2022. He remained a regular heading into this tournament but would ultimately start only one game in a campaign that came to an end at the hands of Belgium in the last 16. “In every career you have moments where you’re a bit down, and you’re a bit in your head about things. I think the World Cup was definitely that for me,” Weah says. “On a personal level, I had to take a back seat and figure out where my place was in the squad.”.
